newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN demands Afghans release French aid workers.
newsitem.headline: UN demands Afghans release French aid workers.

text.p: U.N. Security Council members on Tuesday demanded Afghanistan's purist Taleban leaders immediately release two French aid workers arrested after they sought safety in U.N. headquarters.

The 15-member body at an informal meeting "strongly denounced the violation" of U.N. premises and "demanded the immediate release" of the two Frenchmen from the Paris-based charity, Action Contre la Faim (Action Against Hunger).
"They are deeply concerned about the violence against members of a humanitarian organisation," said the current council president, Ambassador Njuguna Mahugu of Kenya.

The Frenchmen were detained after a series of incidents in which the Taleban militia that controls Kabul, the capital, stormed into a house and the U.N. compound. On Friday, they forcibly searched an ACF house after Afghan women who failed to cover their faces with veils attended a party for one of the group's foreign women members.

The Taleban apparently struck an ACF expatriate woman in the stomach, took away a male cook and his assistant and later were reported to have detained two Afghan women also. The ACF foreign staff then sought refuge in the U.N. compound and armed Taleban militia entered the premises and demanded the arrest of the two Frenchmen, Frederic Michel and Jose Daniel Llorente. They managed to pick them up a day later while they were leaving the compound.
Taleban officials said the Frenchmen had violated Islamic morality and U.N. sources said they told the United Nations to stay out of the affair, which is being handled by France.

But U.N. spokesman Juan-Carlos Brandt said Norbert Holl of Germany, the U.N. special representative in Afghanistan, had protested the detention anyway. He warned that the Taleban could lose aid from private relief groups and would further tarnish its image if the Frenchmen were not released.

The militia, which seized Kabul last September, apparently objected to men and women in the same compound, even though aid officials said they slept in different buildings. The Taleban has imposed strict Islamic law, banning women from the workplace and forcing them to wear veils over their faces.
The group has not been recognised by the United Nations or any other world body as Afghanistan's government.
